whose: OpenAI Codex, under L66, from the sealed corpus

sentences.1: Natural selection acts on whatever is copied faithfully across generations, and in living things that is the gene.
sentences.2: A group is not copied; it dissolves and reforms with every generation, so it cannot be the thing that selection preserves.
sentences.3: Helping spreads when the gene for helping is more likely to be found in the recipients of the help than in the population at large, because then the help lands on copies of itself.
sentences.4: Relatives are the usual case: a helper's kin carry the gene with a known likelihood, and the help pays for itself when the benefit to them, weighted by that likelihood, exceeds the cost.
sentences.5: What looks like selection between groups is this same process seen from a distance, because groups of relatives are exactly where copies of the gene are clustered.
sentences.6: Any accounting in terms of groups can be rewritten in terms of the gene's likelihood of meeting itself, and gives the same answer, so the group adds no cause of its own.
sentences.7: Where a supposed group advantage cannot be so rewritten, it does not spread, because within each group the non-helper still outbreeds the helper and migration mixes the groups faster than the group advantage can act.
sentences.8: Wherever cooperation has spread, as in the social insects and the cell, the members were kin or the copies were bound together so that they could not defect.
sentences.9: The group description is a way of showing the outcome, not a cause that produced it.
sentences.10: Groups are therefore not selected; genes are, and groups are among the places where their copies happen to meet.

leftover: Sentence 2: “with every generation, so it cannot be the thing that selection preserves” — Frequency/time and impossibility are outside the language. Not being copied is kept; inability to be preserved is not silently converted to an actual nonselection claim.

Sentence 3: “Helping spreads when the gene for helping is more likely to be found in the recipients of the help than in the population at large, because then the help lands on copies of itself.” — The helping-spread condition compares likelihoods; its BECAUSE depends on that comparison. No unconditional spread or arrival at copies is asserted by this conditional.

Sentence 4: “Relatives are the usual case: a helper's kin carry the gene with a known likelihood, and the help pays for itself when the benefit to them, weighted by that likelihood, exceeds the cost.” — The kin example depends on probabilistic carriage and a benefit-times-likelihood versus cost inequality. The language has neither probabilities nor amounts; no universal kin-carriage assertion is substituted.

Sentence 5: “What looks like; seen from a distance; exactly where” — Appearance, viewpoint and location are not checked. The identification of processes is retained as an opaque relational fact, not a proved mathematical equivalence.

Sentence 6: “Any accounting in terms of groups can be rewritten in terms of the gene's likelihood of meeting itself, and gives the same answer, so” — Modal rewriteability, probability and arithmetic equivalence are not represented; the stated inference from them to line h consequently has no executable reason line.

Sentence 7: “Where a supposed group advantage cannot be so rewritten, it does not spread; faster than the group advantage can act” — The conditional has a modal/arithmetic antecedent, and the causal comparison is about relative speed. The conditional nonspread conclusion and joint causal relation stay in the bin; i and j retain only separately asserted generic descriptions, not measured effects.

Sentence 8: “could not defect; so that” — Inability and the purpose of binding cannot be analysed. bound_without_defection is an opaque description of the second required alternative; it supplies no modal law. The restriction is represented as an only-ways line, not as an assertion of either disjunct.
Sentence 10: “groups are among the places where their copies happen to meet” — Location is outside the language; no new event or encounter is inferred.

readings: Sentence 1. Open readings: a causal production law or a criterion for what counts as selected. Chosen: SHOWS; b is the writer's identification of the faithfully copied item, not a premise that restates gene selection.
Sentence 5. Open readings: because as production or evidence for identifying two descriptions. Chosen: SINCE, marked filled in; both named process descriptions stay distinct.

Sentence 7. Open readings: conditional scope over all clauses or an asserted reason supporting the conditional. Chosen: i and j are the reason clauses asserted by the writer; the conditional conclusion remains binned.
Sentence 8. Open readings: assert either alternative or record a necessary disjunction. Chosen: only-ways; no disjunct is chosen and no actual defection claim is added.

Sentence 10. Open readings: therefore points to the whole paragraph or the immediately preceding causal rejection. Chosen: h is my reason pointer. In the corrected execution, neg(...) aliases are gated by the same negative source lines h/q; no positive selection/cause inference is tested.
